chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), 'What is your view, if I needed a physician and he was a Christian, should I greet him and supplicate for him?' He said, 'Yes, but your supplication will not benefit him.'
ai.seo_question: Should I greet and make dua for a non-Muslim doctor?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) permits greeting and supplicating for a Christian physician, clarifying that the supplication serves as a social courtesy or for the supplicant's benefit rather than ensuring the physician's spiritual acceptance. This ruling highlights the Shia principle of *adab* (etiquette) in professional interactions, distinguishing between general benevolence and specific theological merit. It reflects the practical flexibility of the Imams in engaging with non-Muslims in contexts of necessity and mutual respect.
